DISCUSSION
There are two types of DC motor speed controls: Amplitude Control and Time Control. C Motor Controllers Amplitude Time Control Control
On DC motors that use amplitude control, varying E (the applied voltage) changes the speed (RPM) of the motor.
In this lesson you will be concerned with Time Control of DC motors.
Time control is based on a duty cycle of repetitive waveforms.
Let's look at using a square wave input to a DC motor first.
A DC motor responds to the average DC voltage applied. If a pure DC signal is applied, the average voltage is the peak value.
Average voltage = E ( time on cycle time ) = 10 ( 0.10 ) = 1VV
When applying a square wave, the average voltage is less than a DC level. Therefore the RPM is also less.
Average Voltage = Duty Cycle x Max Applied Voltage
The average DC voltage is the product of the duty cycle of the wave and the maximum output voltage.
Average voltage = E ( time on cycle time ) = 10 ( 0.10 ) = 1VV
The duty cycle is the ratio of the ON time to the total cycle.
Average voltage = E ( time on cycle time ) = 10 ( .9 ) = 9VVVV
The greater the ON time of the pulse, the higher the average DC voltage and the faster the motor RPM.
This technique is for pulsed waveforms only and is called Pulse Width Modulation, (PWM).
The motor does not stop when the pulse is low (OFF)........
The motor's internal inertia and mass keeps the rotor spinning during OFF times.

Two components that are commonly used to control the firing angle of a signal are an SCR and a TRIAC.
An SCR is a diode that conducts on one alternation of a full cycle, 180
The difference in a SCR is that the point where conduction starts can be varied by a signal applied to the gate.
Even if forward biased, the SCR will not conduct until a voltage is applied to the gate.
The SCR's firing voltage can easily be controlled with a variable resistor. . -
FIRING VOLTAGE - The firing voltage of an SCR is the amount of voltage needed to let the SCR conduct. This voltage is also termed the THRESHOLD VOLTAGE.
